Subject: Discovery recap & next steps — Redwood Inference / Acme Enterprise

Hi Jordan — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap of what we covered and suggested next steps so we have a shared record.

Pain points you called out:
- High per-token costs for interactive assistants (prototype on OpenAI) when scaled to production usage
- Tail latency spikes during peak hours — impacts customer-facing chat SLAs
- Inconsistent throughput across regions and lack of predictable reserved capacity
- Internal compliance: need SOC 2 evidence, VPC/private deployment options, and KMS integration

Current stack you described:
- Prototype built on OpenAI for generation + internal vector store for embeddings (self-hosted)
- Kubernetes-based microservices fronting the model endpoints
- Observability via Datadog; recent incidents around autoscale lag

Success criteria you shared:
- 99th pct latency for chat < 200ms (for typical prompts)
- Cost per 1M tokens within target band (we discussed a goal of ~25-40% below current spend)
- Predictable throughput of ~200 qps with burst handling and cross-region failover
- SOC 2 evidence and ability to run in a VPC/private deployment for sensitive traffic

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) Redwood to send an initial sizing + architecture proposal and a back-of-envelope cost estimate (attached: initial-benchmarks.csv, redwood-product-one-pager.pdf) — owner: me, ETA: 3 business days
2) Confirm procurement and legal contacts and expected timeline for vendor evaluation — can you introduce procurement?
3) Technical follow-up: quick 30m call with our solutions engineer (Dev) to validate performance assumptions and discuss pilot scope — suggested window next week

Procurement framing: to keep momentum, it helps if we surface the decision process up front (timeline, stakeholders, PO process, contract guards). If you’re open to it, please share the names/roles of anyone who will be evaluating (legal, procurement, security, engineering lead).

Attachments: redwood-product-one-pager.pdf, initial-benchmarks.csv

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Jordan / Procurement team — thanks for the quick turnaround and for looping procurement in. Added Dev (solutions engineering) and Lauren (my manager) to help with sizing and procurement questions.

Procurement framing (initial guardrails to unblock evaluation):
- Preferred commercial paths for pilots: 1) Hosted API with committed spend discount (monthly commit) OR 2) Dedicated reserved capacity (1–12 month trial capacity agreement) depending on your security needs.
- Typical pilot commercial guardrails we recommend:
  * Pilot term: 1–3 months
  * Reserved commit (if Dedicated): small footprint (e.g., 1-2 GPU nodes) to validate throughput/latency before upsizing
  * Price band: we’ll provide a scoped estimate but expect a meaningful discount on committed usage vs ad-hoc usage pricing
- Contract levers procurement often asks for up front: SLA terms (availability/latency credits), data residency commitments, incident response SLAs, and audit evidence (SOC 2 report). We have a standard package (attaching procurement-checklist.xlsx and redwood-sla.pdf) that maps those items to required artifacts.

Action items from Redwood (next 3 business days):
- Deliver a 1-page proposal: recommended pilot architecture (hosted vs dedicated), estimated cost range, and proposed pilot KPIs (owner: Marissa)
- Schedule 30m technical sync with Dev to scope pilot inputs and acceptance tests — Dev, suggest Tue/Thu next week windows?
- Share contract & procurement checklist for your legal/procurement review (attached)

Jordan — can you confirm the procurement PO flow (does Acme require an initial SOW/PO prior to pilot spend) and whether a deal champion (you or Maya) will be authorized to sign a pilot/order? That will help us align the pricing/commitment language.

Thanks — looping in attachments: procurement-checklist.xlsx, redwood-sla.pdf

Jordan — thanks for the context. A few technical clarifications to make the pilot estimate more accurate:

- Can you share a sample prompt distribution (avg tokens per request, top-10 patterns) and expected concurrency during peak? Even rough numbers help a lot.
- Data residency: if any traffic must remain in a VPC/on-prem path, we should scope Dedicated/Private pilot vs hosted.
- Latency acceptance test: propose a scripted test set (50 representative prompts) run at 2 concurrency levels (50 qps, 200 qps) to validate 99th pct latency. We’ll also produce a KV/prefix-caching plan to improve tail latency.

Proposed pilot scope (high level):
- Duration: 4 weeks
- Environment: Hosted with committed monthly spend OR Dedicated single-node trial (we’ll recommend based on your compliance needs)
- Acceptance: 99th pct latency < 200ms on representative set; end-to-end functional smoke tests pass

I’ll prepare a short tech appendix to attach to Marissa’s 1-pager. Happy to take the sync Tue/Thu next week — I’m available Tue 10–12 PT and Thu 9–11 PT.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
